paragraphs: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc. ("Holdings"), through its direct and indirect subsidiaries, including American Multi-Cinema, Inc. ("Multi-Cinema") and its subsidiaries, (collectively with Holdings, unless the context otherwise requires, the "Company" or "AMC"), is principally involved in the theatrical exhibition business and owns, operates or has interests in theatres located in the United States and Europe.

Our business was founded in Kansas City, Missouri in 1920. Holdings was incorporated under the laws of the state of Delaware on June 6, 2007. We maintain our principal executive offices at One AMC Way, 11500 Ash Street, Leawood, Kansas 66211.
As of December 31, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $428.5 million.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, we took action to lower the future interest expense of our fixed-rate debt through debt buybacks and exchanges for equity and enhanced liquidity through equity issuances. See Note 7—Corporate Borrowings and Finance Lease Liabilities, Note 8—Stockholders' Deficit, and Note 14—Subsequent Events in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements under Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K, for further information regarding equity issuances and debt repurchases and exchanges.

On July 24, 2025, Muvico, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company ("Muvico"), issued $857.0 million aggregate principal amount of new Senior Secured Notes due 2029 (the "New 2029 Notes") in exchange for $590.0 million aggregate principal amount of 7.5% First Lien Senior Secured Notes due 2029 ("Existing 7.5% Notes") and $244.4 million of incremental, new money financing. On the same day, Muvico also issued $194.4 million aggregate principal amount of New Exchangeable Notes in exchange for $194.4 million aggregate principal amount of Existing Exchangeable Notes. On September 30, 2025, $39.9 million aggregate principal of New Exchangeable Notes were cancelled pursuant to a downward adjustment feature in the New Exchangeable Notes, which represented the maximum possible downward adjustment. We used the new money financing from the issuance of the New 2029 Notes to fully redeem our outstanding 5.875% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2026 (the "Senior Subordinated Notes due 2026") and our 10%/12% Cash/PIK Toggle Second Lien Subordinated Secured Notes due 2026 (the "Second Lien Notes") and also to pay consent fees to the Consenting Term Loan Lenders (as defined herein).

The New Exchangeable Notes were not initially exchangeable into Common Stock. At the 2025 Annual Meeting, our stockholders approved an amendment to the Company's Certificate of Incorporation for the Authorized Share Increase which allowed for the New Exchangeable Notes to become exchangeable and lowered the interest rate to 1.5% cash interest. The Authorized Share increase also allowed for a $15.0 million consent fee payable to Consenting Existing Exchangeable Noteholders to be payable in the form of shares of Common Stock, based on a price determined based on the average of the daily volume weighted average price of our Common Stock for the sixty consecutive trading days commencing on December 22, 2025. On December 22, 2025, the Company and the holders of the New Exchangeable Notes agreed to amend the New Exchangeable Notes Indenture, among other things, to amend and restate the Exchange Rate and allow for up to $150.0 million of net proceeds from sales of at-the-market offerings. The amendments were memorialized in a supplemental indenture dated January 12, 2026 (the "New Exchangeable Notes Supplemental Indenture"). As consideration for the indenture amendments the Company will pay the New Exchangeable Noteholders a consent fee of $6.25 million payable in shares of Common Stock. The number of shares will be based on the average of the daily volume weighted average price of our Common Stock for the sixty consecutive trading days commencing on December 22, 2025.

See Note 7—Corporate Borrowings and Finance Lease Liabilities and Note—14 Subsequent Events in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements under Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K for further information regarding these transactions.

We expect, from time to time, to continue to seek to retire or purchase our outstanding debt through cash purchases and/or exchanges for equity or debt, in open-market purchases, privately negotiated transactions or otherwise. We continuously monitor the capital markets and our capital structure, and may, from time to time, seek to refinance, amend or otherwise restructure our outstanding debt on an opportunistic basis. Such repurchases, refinancings, amendments, restructurings or exchanges, if any, will be upon such terms and at such prices as we may determine, and will depend on prevailing market conditions, our liquidity requirements, the availability of authorized share capital, contractual restrictions and other factors. The amounts involved may be material, and to the extent equity is used, dilutive. For example, on February 17, 2026, we launched a financing transaction (the "Financing Transaction") to refinance the New Term Loans and Odeon Notes due 2027 (in each case as defined herein). There can be no assurance that we will successfully enter into an agreement with respect to or complete the Financing Transaction, which is subject to, among other things, market and other conditions, and the negotiation and execution of definitive documents.

We are the world's largest theatrical exhibition company and an industry leader in innovation and operational excellence. Over the course of our 100+ year history, we have pioneered many of the theatrical exhibition industry's most important innovations. We introduced multiplex theatres in the 1960s and the North American stadium-seated megaplex theatre format in the 1990s. Most recently, we continued to innovate and evolve the movie-going experience with the deployment of our theatre renovations featuring plush, powered recliner seating and the launch of our U.S. subscription loyalty tier, AMC Stubs® A-List ("A-List"). Our growth has been driven by a combination of organic growth through reinvestment in our existing assets and through the acquisition of some of the most significant companies in the theatrical exhibition industry.

Our business is operated in two theatrical exhibition reportable segments, U.S. markets and International markets. Substantially all of our international operations are attributed to Odeon Cinemas Group Limited ("OCGL") and its subsidiaries, Odeon and UCI Cinemas Holdings Limited ("Odeon") and Nordic Cinema Group Holding AB ("Nordic").

As of December 31, 2025, we owned, leased or operated 855 theatres and 9,640 screens in 11 countries, including 533 theatres with a total of 7,072 screens in the United States and 322 theatres and 2,568 screens in European markets. We have productive assets in each of the capital cities and most densely populated areas of the countries in which we operate.

As of December 31, 2025, we were the market leader in the United States and Europe including in Sweden, Norway, and Finland, and a leading theatre operator in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Germany. We have operations in four of the world's 10 largest economies, including four of the six largest European economies (the United Kingdom, Spain, Italy and Germany) as of December 31, 2025.

As of December 31, 2025, in the U.S. markets, we owned, leased or operated theatres in 41 states and the District of Columbia, with approximately 49% of the U.S. population living within 10 miles of one of our theatres. We have a diversified footprint with complementary global geographic and guest demographic profiles, which we believe gives our circuit a unique profile and offers us strategic and operational advantages while providing our studio partners with a large and diverse distribution channel. We operate some of the most productive theatres in the top markets in the United States and were the market leader in the top two markets for the year ended December 31, 2025: Los Angeles and New York. During 2025, our top five markets, in each of which we held the #1 share position, were New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Atlanta, and Washington DC according to data provided by Comscore.

paragraphs: The following is a summary list of risk factors:

● absent significant increases in revenues and attendance, our ability to obtain additional liquidity, which if not realized or is insufficient, likely would result in us seeking an in-court or out-of-court restructuring of our liabilities, and in the event of such future liquidation or bankruptcy proceeding, holders of our Common Stock and other securities would likely suffer a total loss of their investment;

● our substantial level of indebtedness and our current liquidity constraints could adversely affect our financial condition and our ability to service our indebtedness, to pre-pay debt, and to refinance debt and to do so with comparable interest rates or other favorable terms, and our ability to take advantage of certain business opportunities, which could negatively impact the ability of investors to recover their investment in our Common Stock;
● risks relating to impairment losses, including with respect to goodwill and other intangibles, and theatre and other closure charges;
● limitations on the availability of capital or poor financial results may prevent us from deploying strategic initiatives; and

● we are currently not paying dividends and in the future may not generate sufficient cash flows or have sufficient restricted payment capacity under the indentures governing our debt securities to pay dividends on our Common Stock.

AMC is the world's largest theatrical exhibition company and an industry leader in innovation and operational excellence. As of December 31, 2025 we operated in 11 countries including the United States and throughout Europe.

Our theatrical exhibition revenues are generated primarily from box office admissions and food and beverage sales. The balance of our revenues is generated from ancillary sources, including online ticketing fees, on-screen advertising, income from gift card and exchange ticket sales, rental of theatre auditoriums, retail popcorn and merchandise sales, fees earned from our customer loyalty programs, and theatrical distribution. As of December 31, 2025, we owned, operated or had interests in 855 theatres and 9,640 screens.

2025 Debt Refinancing and Additional Share Authorization. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we completed a series of refinancing transactions with certain holders of our Existing 7.5% Notes, certain holders of the Existing Exchangeable Notes, and certain lenders of our term loans outstanding under our credit agreement. Additionally, at the 2025 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on December 10, 2025, the Company's stockholders approved an amendment to the Company's certificate of incorporation to increase the total number of authorized shares of the Company's Common Stock from 550,000,000 to 1,100,000,000 shares of Common Stock. The increase in authorized shares allows for, among other things, the potential conversion of the Company's New Exchangeable Notes that were issued as part of the refinancing transactions. See Note 7—Corporate Borrowings and Finance Lease Liabilities in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements under Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K for further information regarding these transactions.

NCM ESA Amendment. On April 17, 2025, NCM (as defined herein) entered into the Amended ESA (as defined herein) with the Company. The term of the Amended ESA has been extended by five years through February 13, 2042. We treated the Amended ESA as a contract modification pursuant to ASC 606 – Revenue from Contracts with Customers. Accordingly, we have allocated the additional consideration received from the contract modification to the exhibitor services agreement contract liability and updated the discount rate used to account for the significant financing component to 16.12%. Prior to the contract modification, the weighted average discount rate used to account for the significant financing component was approximately 7.5%. The contract liability will be reclassified to other theatre revenue over the new term of the Amended ESA as the remaining performance obligations are satisfied. Concurrently with entering into the Amended ESA, NCM and the Company reached an agreement to, among other things, dismiss with prejudice the ongoing litigation between the parties.

paragraphs: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Inc. ("Holdings"), 透過其直接及間接子公司，包括 American Multi-Cinema, Inc. ("Multi-Cinema") 及其子公司，(與 Holdings 合併計算，除非文意另有明確說明，為 "Company" 或 "AMC")，主要從事電影院經營業務，並擁有、營運或持有美國與歐洲地區的電影院資產。
我們的業務起源於美國密蘇裏州堪薩斯城，於 1920 年成立。Holdings 於 2007 年 6 月 6 日根據特拉華州法律註冊成立。我們的總部辦公室設於 One AMC Way, 11500 Ash Street, Leawood, Kansas 66211。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們持有現金及現金等價物約 428.5 百萬美元。

在 2025 年度結算期間，我們透過債務買回及交換為股權，以降低未來固定利率債務的利息支出，並透過發行股權增強流動性。有關股權發行及債務買回與交換的進一步資訊，請參閱本 Form 10-K 第二部，第 8 項「財務會計資訊」附註中的 Note 7—Corporate Borrowings and Finance Lease Liabilities、Note 8—Stockholders' Deficit 及 Note 14—Subsequent Events。

2025 年 7 月 24 日，Muvico, LLC，為本公司之 wholly-owned subsidiary ("Muvico")，發行總金額為 857.0 百萬美元的新高階有擔保貸款 ("New 2029 Notes")，以交換 590.0 百萬美元總金額之 7.5% 第一順位高階有擔保貸款 ("Existing 7.5% Notes") 及 244.4 百萬美元之新增資金。同日，Muvico 亦發行總金額為 194.4 百萬美元之新可轉換貸款 ("New Exchangeable Notes")，以交換總金額為 194.4 百萬美元之現有可轉換貸款 ("Existing Exchangeable Notes")。2025 年 9 月 30 日，根據新可轉換貸款之向下調整條款，取消總金額為 39.9 百萬美元之新可轉換貸款，此為該條款所允許之最大向下調整。我們使用新可轉換貸款發行所得之新增資金，以完全贖回我們尚未償還之 5.875% 高階次級貸款 ("Senior Subordinated Notes due 2026") 及 10%/12% 現金/PIK Toggle 第二順位次級有擔保貸款 ("Second Lien Notes")，並支付同意貸款人 (Consenting Term Loan Lenders) 之同意費用。

新可轉換貸款最初不可轉換為普通股。於 2025 年年度股東大會，我們股東批准本公司章程之授權股份增加，允許新可轉換貸款轉換為普通股，並將利率降低至 1.5% 現金利率。授權股份增加亦允許支付 15.0 百萬美元之同意費用給現有可轉換貸款持有人，該費用可透過根據 2025 年 12 月 22 日起連續六十個交易日之普通股每日成交量加權平均價格之平均值計算之普通股股份支付。2025 年 12 月 22 日，本公司與新可轉換貸款持有人同意修改新可轉換貸款之 indenture，其中包含修改及重述轉換率，並允許最多 150.0 百萬美元之淨資金來自市場現金發行。此等修改於 2026 年 1 月 12 日之補充 indenture ("New Exchangeable Notes Supplemental Indenture") 中記載。作為 indenture 修改之對價，本公司將向新可轉換貸款持有人支付 6.25 百萬美元之同意費用，以普通股股份支付。股份數量將根據 2025 年 12 月 22 日起連續六十個交易日之普通股每日成交量加權平均價格之平均值計算。
有關這些交易之進一步資訊，請參閱本 Form 10-K 第二部，第 8 項「財務會計資訊」附註中的 Note 7—Corporate Borrowings and Finance Lease Liabilities 及 Note 14—Subsequent Events。

我們預期，不時會繼續尋求透過現金買回及/或交換為股權或債務，以償還或購買我們尚未償還之債務，方式包括公開市場買回、私下協議交易或其他方式。我們持續監測資本市場及我們之資本結構，並可能不時根據機會主義方式尋求重新融資、修改或重新安排我們尚未償還之債務。任何買回、重新融資、修改、重新安排或交換，如有，將根據我們所決定之條件及價格進行，並取決於市場狀況、我們之流動性需求、已授權股份資本之可得性、契約限制及其他因素。涉及金額可能重大，且若使用股權，將導致稀釋。例如，2026 年 2 月 17 日，我們啟動一項融資交易 ("Financing Transaction")，以重新融資 2027 年到期之新貸款及 Odeon 貸款 (在各項定義中)。無法保證我們將成功與對方達成協議或完成此融資交易，該交易受市場及其他條件，以及最終協議文件之談判及簽訂之限制。

本公司為全球最大的戲院展演公司，並在創新與運營卓越方面為產業領導者。在超過百年的歷史中，我們已發明許多戲院展演產業最重要的創新。我們於1960年代引入多廳戲院，並於1990年代推出北美體育座式巨幕戲院格式。最近，我們持續創新並進化電影觀賞體驗，透過部署我們的戲院翻新工程，提供舒適、可調節的躺椅座位，並推出美國訂閱忠誠度層級，AMC Stubs® A-List ("A-List")。我們的成長是由於透過對現有資產的再投資以及收購戲院展演產業中一些最重要的公司而來的有機成長。
本公司業務分為兩個戲院展演應報告分部，美國市場與國際市場。我們國際業務幾乎全部歸屬於Odeon Cinemas Group Limited ("OCGL")及其子公司，Odeon and UCI Cinemas Holdings Limited ("Odeon")以及Nordic Cinema Group Holding AB ("Nordic")。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有、租賃或經營855間戲院與9,640個銀幕，分佈於11個國家，包括美國533間戲院，總共7,072個銀幕，以及歐洲市場322間戲院與2,568個銀幕。我們在每個我們經營的國家的首都與人口最密集地區均有生產性資產。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司為美國與歐洲市場的領導者，包括瑞典、挪威與芬蘭，並為英國、愛爾蘭、義大利、西班牙、葡萄牙與德國的主要戲院經營者。我們在四個世界十大經濟體中經營業務，包括截至2025年12月31日的六個最大歐洲經濟體（英國、西班牙、義大利與德國）。

截至2025年12月31日，在美國市場，本公司擁有、租賃或經營41個州與華盛頓特區的戲院，約有49%的美國人口居住在距離我們戲院10英里內。我們有廣泛的分佈，具有補充性的全球地理與觀眾人口統計資料，我們認為這使我們的戲院網路具有獨特的特色，並提供我們戰略與運營優勢，同時為我們的電影製片夥伴提供廣大且多樣的發行渠道。我們經營美國主要市場中一些最具生產力的戲院，並在截至2025年12月31日的年度中，為洛杉磯與紐約這兩個主要市場的領導者。根據Comscore提供的資料，2025年我們前五大市場，每個市場我們均為市場第一，為紐約、洛杉磯、芝加哥、亞特蘭大與華盛頓特區。

paragraphs: 以下討論內容係關於 AMC 合併會計財務報表，包含於本年度報告表 10-K 其他部分。此討論內容包含前瞻性陳述。請參閱本年度報告表 10-K 第 I 部分之「前瞻性陳述」及「風險因素」，以瞭解與這些陳述相關之風險、不確定性及假設。請參閱本表 10-K 第 II 部分，第 8 項「合併財務報表附註」中之附註 1—本公司及重要會計政策，以取得有關本公司重要會計政策之資訊。
AMC 為全球最大的電影院經營公司，並在創新與運營卓越方面為產業領導者。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在 11 個國家運營，包括美國及歐洲各地。
我們的電影院經營收入主要來自票房收入及餐飲銷售。我們收入的其餘部分來自輔助來源，包括線上售票費用、螢幕廣告收入、禮品卡及換票銷售收入、電影院劇場租賃收入、零售爆米花及商品銷售收入、來自我們客戶忠誠度計畫之費用收入，以及電影發行收入。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有、營運或持有權益的電影院數量為 855 家，銀幕數量為 9,640 個。

2025 年債務重新融資及新增普通股授權。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之會計年度內，我們完成了與部分現有 7.5% 記息債券持有人、部分現有可轉換債券持有人，以及部分我們信用協議下現有過橋貸款貸款人之一系列重新融資交易。此外，於 2025 年 12 月 10 日舉行之年度股東大會上，本公司股東批准修改本公司章程，將本公司普通股總發行數量從 550,000,000 股增至 1,100,000,000 股。增加發行數量允許，除其他事項外，本公司新發行可轉換債券之潛在轉換。請參閱本表 10-K 第 II 部分，第 8 項「合併財務報表附註」中之附註 7—企業借款及財務租賃負債，以取得有關這些交易之進一步資訊。

NCM ESA 修改協議。2025 年 4 月 17 日，NCM（如本處所定義）與本公司簽訂了修改後之 ESA（如本處所定義）。修改後之 ESA 合約期間已延長五年至 2042 年 2 月 13 日。我們將修改後之 ESA 視為根據 ASC 606—與客戶之合約收入之合約修改。因此，我們已將因合約修改所收到之額外對價分配至展商服務協議合約負債，並更新用以會計處理重大融資成分之折現率為 16.12%。在合約修改前，用以會計處理重大融資成分之加權平均折現率約為 7.5%。合約負債將在修改後 ESA 新合約期間內，隨著剩餘履行義務之完成重新歸類至其他電影院收入。同時，NCM 與本公司達成協議，除其他事項外，並同意終止雙方之間持續進行之訴訟。
此外，於截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之會計年度內，本公司透過「市場現貨」發行方式發行普通股。下述表格總結了「市場現貨」發行之活動：

債務買回與交換。下表總結了在2024年12月31日為結業年度內發生的各種現金債務買回交易、債務換股交易，以及現金與債務換股交易。債務換股交易被視為債務提前清償。根據ASC 470-50-40-3，清償債務的重新取得價格被認定為交換所得普通股的公允價值。請參閱本表10-K申報書第二部分，第8項「公司借款與財務租賃負債」之附註，以取得這些交易之更多資訊。

headings: 與我們股票相關的風險
我們可能因未來商譽、其他無形資產或長期資產減損，或未來劇院及其他關閉而產生未來減損費用。
資本可取得性受到限制，以及資本支出減少，可能會延誤或阻止戰略計畫的執行。
我們的業務依賴電影製造與演出，並面臨激烈的競爭，包括替代性電影傳輸方式增加或其他形式娛樂的出現。
我們依賴電影分發商來分發我們所放映的電影，而我們對這些分發商毫無控制權，若我們無法取得或延遲取得電影，可能會對我們的業務造成不利影響。
本公司營運成果將受電影獨佔上映窗口縮短及其他電影業者採用之做法影響。
本公司目前及未來表現依賴關鍵人員。
供應鏈中斷、勞工短缺及通貨膨脹可能對本公司營運及營運成果產生負面影響。
透過新興建設及現有戲院之轉型來優化戲院路線，可能面臨延誤及未預見之成本。
氣候變遷、惡劣天氣條件及天然災害可能對本公司戲院營運、銷售或財務成果產生負面影響。
本公司正在將人工智能技術應用於部分營運，此舉可能產生營運及聲譽風險。
本公司在顧客體驗及營運中應用人工智能技術，可能產生風險敞口，影響本公司營運表現。
總體政治、社會及經濟條件可能降低本公司營運收入及入場人數。
本公司受重大政府規範管制，可能產生重大成本。
規範我們國際業務運作的法律體系，可能要求我們國際子公司或其董事進行破產程序。
本公司可能被反壟斷機關審查。
本公司業務受國際經濟、政治及其他風險影響，可能對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況產生負面影響。
與本公司發行股份相關的風險
本公司已出現顯著的稀釋，且未來可能持續有額外的稀釋，這可能對本公司普通股的市場價格產生負面影響。

paragraphs: 以下為風險因素之總結清單：
● 若缺乏顯著增加之營業收入與入場人數，本公司取得額外流動性之能力，若無法實現或不足，將很可能導致本公司尋求法院內或法院外之債務重整，若發生未來清算或破產程序，本公司普通股及其他證券之持有人將很可能喪失其全部投資；
● 本公司負擔之高額債務及目前流動性限制，可能不利於本公司財務狀況及償還債務、提前償還債務、重新融資債務之能力，且可能無法以相同利率或其他有利條件進行，亦可能影響本公司把握特定商業機會之能力，此將可能不利於投資人回收其在本公司普通股之投資；
● 與減損損失相關之風險，包括與商譽及其他無形資產，以及劇場及其他關閉費用相關之風險；
● 資本可取得性之限制或財務結果不佳，可能導致本公司無法執行戰略性計畫；以及
● 本公司目前未發放股息，未來可能無法產生足夠之現金流或根據債務證券之抵押契約，具足夠之受限支付能力以發放普通股股息。
